_comment: Maps the evidence-store's own protection mechanisms to the FedRAMP 20x / NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 control identifiers they support. This is what turns 'we have WORM + signatures' into 'we can show an assessor which control each mechanism supports'. Every control id here was verified verbatim against references/fedramp-consolidated-rules.json. This is a traceability aid and an advisory mapping; it is NOT a compliance determination - the assessor decides whether a control is met. AU-10 (Non-repudiation) appears in the CR26 Rev5 controls list at the higher class only; it is scoped accordingly below.
scope: The durable evidence/metric-history store provisioned by automation/storage/provision_store.py and the evidence signatures produced by automation/collectors/sign_evidence.py.

mechanisms.rationale: Every write retains prior versions, so an audit record cannot be silently replaced and history is recoverable. AU-09 protects audit information from unauthorized modification; AU-11 requires audit-record retention.

mechanisms.mechanism: S3 Object Lock (WORM), GOVERNANCE or COMPLIANCE mode with default retention
mechanisms.rationale: Write-once storage makes an audit record immutable for the retention period. COMPLIANCE mode cannot be shortened even by root, giving genuine write-once protection of audit information (AU-09 and its stored-integrity enhancements) and enforced retention (AU-11).
mechanisms.caveat: COMPLIANCE mode is an operational commitment: records cannot be deleted before the retention period expires, by anyone including the account root. Choose the mode deliberately.

mechanisms.mechanism: KMS asymmetric signature over the evidence content hash
mechanisms.rationale: The signature is produced by a SEPARATE signer principal whose key the read-only collector cannot reach (kms:Sign denied to the collector role). It provides non-repudiation of the evidence digest: a privileged actor who rewrites the record store still cannot forge the signature without kms:Sign. AU-09 (02)/(03)/(04) cover cryptographic and separate-storage protection of audit information; AU-10 covers non-repudiation.
mechanisms.class_applicability: AU-10 is in the CR26 Rev5 controls list at the higher assurance class; AU-09 and its enhancements apply across classes. Signing supports both, but only claim AU-10 where the class profile requires it.
mechanisms.boundary: The non-repudiation property holds ONLY when the signer principal is genuinely outside the collector's and the assessed account's blast radius (see evidence-store-isolation reference). If the same admin holds both, the trust is moved, not removed.

mechanisms.mechanism: Least-privilege, separately-logged access to the evidence store
mechanisms.provided_by: automation/storage/DEPLOY.md (least-privilege deploy profile) + evidence-store-isolation reference stack
mechanisms.rationale: Access to log/evidence data is least-privileged and access to the store is managed separately from the accounts being assessed. KSI-MLA-ALA (Authorizing Log Access) requires a least-privileged, role/attribute-based, just-in-time access model for log data; AU-09 (04) covers access by a subset of privileged users.
mechanisms.class_applicability: KSI-MLA-ALA is Optional at Class B and required at Class C per the dataset varies_by_class; scope the claim to the class.

mechanisms.mechanism: Content hash (SHA-256) over the sanitized source fact
mechanisms.rationale: Tamper-EVIDENCE: a reviewer or CI recomputes the digest to detect a silently-edited evidence object. This alone is not tamper-PROOF against a privileged rewrite (that is what the KMS signature adds), but it supports AU-09 detection of unauthorized modification.

record_retention_note: The CR26 governing window for the KSI metric history (SDR-CSX-KMT) is up to one year; SCN-CSO-MAR requires providers to maintain auditable records of significant-change evaluation activities and make them available to FedRAMP on request. --retention-days is a provider policy choice, not a fixed 7-year default.
